Also report the "announcement window" return you can't catch (prior close to entry) so the uncatchable part is visible.
- Returns: stock minus IWM from entry to the close 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 and 20 sessions later; also beta-adjusted (stock minus beta*IWM, beta from the prior 120 sessions shrunk a third toward 1, as screen.beta does). Report mean, median, hit rate, N events, N distinct dates, t-stat on per-date averages (events cluster), both halves of the sample separately, and the mean net of 100 bp. Long-side events (13D, insider buys) measured as long; distress events (NT filings and the 8-K distress items) reported raw so the sign shows, and as a short.

agents.report:
Only one thing survives the test before costs: insider buying predicts returns against IWM, reliably, in both samples and both halves. But on average it doesn't pay for a 1% round trip. The 13D result is fragile, and the distress filings are about break-even as a short. Most of the distress population is missing from the sample, so their measured decline is too mild.

Each route below gives the move against IWM per entry date, at the entry a pass could get. The two numbers are today's 366 names / the approximate point-in-time sample.

**Insider buying (officers and directors, Form 4 code P)**
- **Before cost:** +83 / +57 bp after one session and +111 / +86 bp after five (|t| 3.2–4.9). It passes the bar (|t| > 3, same sign in both halves) at every horizon from 1 to 5 sessions in both samples.
- **After 100 bp:** about zero. +11 bp at 5 sessions in today's names (t 0.4), −14 bp point-in-time. The median event is near flat (+24 / −6 bp at 5 sessions).
- **The part you can't catch:** +245 / +279 bp of the reaction happens between the prior close and the entry.
- **Two cuts known at entry do clear the cost**, in both samples and both halves:
  - The stock hadn't already gapped more than 2% (about half the triggers): +134 / +174 bp at 5 sessions, net +34 / +74 bp.
  - Two or more insiders buying: +208 / +157 bp, net +108 / +57 bp.
  - Their net-of-cost t is only 0.7–2.0, and I picked them after seeing the data. Treat them as leads for the judge, not an edge.
- **Other splits don't help:** CFO or CEO among the buyers, dollar size (purchases of $1M+ add nothing), distance from the 52-week high, analyst count, a same-day 8-K.

**Filing route**
- **Initial 13D:** +168 to +236 bp at 2–3 sessions point-in-time (t 3.1–3.5), but only t 1.0–1.4 in today's names. Without its five biggest names the 5-session result falls from +211 to +81 bp. Suggestive, not reliable.
- **Distress (NT 10-K/10-Q and the 8-K items):** −103 / −75 bp in the first session. That passes only in today's names (t −3.0), and as a short it nets just +3 to +5 bp, before any borrow fee.
  - Delisting notices (8-K 3.01) fall about −254 bp by 3 sessions point-in-time (t −2.7). In today's names they rebound instead, because the filers still in the band today are the ones that recovered.
  - No single filing type passes the bar.

**Names per session (today's 366 names)**

| route | names per session |
|---|---|
| filing | 0.64 (13D 0.23, delisting notice 0.12, NT 10-Q 0.09) |
| insider triggers | 1.00 (1.54 if follow-on Form 4s count) |
| both, distinct names | about 1.6 |

At least one name comes up on 70% of sessions; the busiest session had 11. The routes almost never overlap: 29 of 1,375 insider triggers had a filing within 5 sessions.

**Main limitations**
- **Missing distress filers.** For comparable companies outside the sample (public float $150M–$1B at the time), the SEC's records show 580 delisting notices against our 91, and 49 bankruptcies against 0. About two thirds of those 580 filers have no ticker today. For the 13D, the missing names include buyouts as well as failures, so the bias there has no clear direction.
- **Entry prices.** Filings made during trading hours are entered at that day's close, because daily bars can't price the 10:30 AM ET / 2:00 PM ET passes. 86% of events came outside hours and are entered at the next open. The 100 bp round trip is an assumption, with no borrow fee on shorts.
- **Approximations.** The point-in-time sample estimates past market value from today's value scaled by price. The analyst count is today's.
- **Many splits.** About 150 rows were tested, so a few |t| > 3 results are expected by chance.
- **Data checks.** The SEC's quarterly insider data sets agreed with the project's own Form 4 parser on owner and role in all 60 sampled filings, and on value within 1.5%. EDGAR's acceptance times are UTC, as the code assumes; I checked two filings against their index pages.

**Screen behaviour you may want to change (not changed):**
- `edgar.events` also counts 13Ds the company filed about someone else: 28 of 776 since 2021. I dropped them here.
- Follow-on Form 4s let an insider name back onto the screen even though they aren't new triggers.

I didn't modify anything else in the repo, touch git, or connect to the gateway.

Files are in research_notes/Small cap screen design:
- filings_insider_backtest.md
- scripts/filings_backtest/
